title: Big Hairy Audacious Goals
coreMove: Set a goal big enough to concentrate progress, but test whether its size serves the core instead of ego, spectacle, or panic.
sourcePressure: The sidecar supports the chapter title, the BHAG label, and the book-wide logic that visionary companies preserve a core while stimulating progress through ambition.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating any huge target as visionary, when a BHAG must focus institutional effort around the core rather than inflate a leader's self-image.

sourceAnchors.name: BHAG
sourceAnchors.detail: the source sidecar says the preview common terms include Audacious Goals and BHAG
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A BHAG is not a large wish; it is a target that turns scattered progress into organized movement.

counterintuition: big goals are not about size
examples: startup announces a huge user number
plant manager with a press-line clock

exampleSpecs.domain: regional blood bank committing to same-day emergency supply across remote hospitals
exampleSpecs.audience: Megan, logistics director facing scattered improvement projects
exampleSpecs.stakes: trauma teams keep improvising because no single target forces the system to change
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 5:55 a.m., Megan writes the same-day target on the route board, then cancels three vanity projects that do not shorten emergency delivery
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a route board with red magnets for remote hospitals

exampleSpecs.domain: regional theatre pledging every youth ticket under ten dollars within three seasons
exampleSpecs.audience: Etienne, executive director balancing access and solvency
exampleSpecs.stakes: audience renewal will fail if access remains a donation slogan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Etienne pins the ten-dollar target above the season budget and makes programming, fundraising, and seating decisions answer to it
exampleSpecs.firstImage: colored seat maps spread below a handwritten ten-dollar note
mustAvoid: arts access language without operating choices

exampleSpecs.domain: industrial laundry aiming for zero rewash loads for hospital linens in one year
exampleSpecs.audience: Paula, quality supervisor whose team is tired of minor fixes
exampleSpecs.stakes: rewash delays can leave wards short and hide infection-control risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Paula asks which machines, shifts, and inspection steps would have to change if zero rewash were real, then turns answers into the year plan
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What would break first if the rewash cart had to stay empty?

exampleSpecs.domain: open-source mapping nonprofit setting a goal to map every rural clinic in a province before flood season
exampleSpecs.audience: Chris, volunteer coordinator with scattered contributors
exampleSpecs.stakes: emergency crews may lack accurate clinic locations during floods
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chris draws the flood-season deadline across the map wall and assigns volunteers by unmapped clinic clusters, not by enthusiasm alone
exampleSpecs.firstImage: pushpins missing from a damp paper map of river towns
mustAvoid: volunteer enthusiasm substitutes for target architecture

exampleSpecs.domain: hotel group promising every room ready by 3 p.m. for a peak-season month
exampleSpecs.audience: Isabel, housekeeping director confronting chronic late check-ins
exampleSpecs.stakes: guest trust and staff morale collapse when the promise is always almost met
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Isabel three Saturdays to see that the 3 p.m. promise forced laundry timing, inspection routes, and front-desk holds into one system
exampleSpecs.firstImage: key cards lined in rows beside a 2:47 p.m. lobby clock

exampleSpecs.domain: urban tree nursery targeting enough native saplings for every heat-island block in five years
exampleSpecs.audience: Aman, nursery planner coordinating city crews and schools
exampleSpecs.stakes: a climate pledge stays symbolic unless the nursery capacity changes now
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Aman count seed trays backward from the five-year block map, then reject a prettier campaign that would not grow enough roots
exampleSpecs.firstImage: seed trays numbered against a wall map of red heat blocks
mustAvoid: environmental aspiration with no capacity math

skillTargets: test whether a large goal organizes real work
distinguish core-serving ambition from ego targets
choose operational consequences that make audacity credible

tryThisNowSpec: Write one large target, then list the three projects it would force you to stop. If it stops nothing, it is probably a slogan.
sourceAnchorsNote: Frozen source sidecars for this book expose concept support and source artifacts, but little chapter-level anecdote detail after chapter 1. Use only the anchors listed here; do not invent company histories, named executives, studies, or dates.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
